note: English subtitles: one entry per Japanese sentence of tour_01227.json (same order), so cues share the Japanese timing.

steps.title: The least populated city
sentences: This is Utashinai, Hokkaido.
In 2020 its population was 2,989.
That is the smallest of any city in Japan.
53 percent of residents are 65 or older, also the highest of any city in Japan.

steps.title: Only 4.7% of the land is livable
sentences: Most of the city is mountains, cut by many deep valleys.
Land gentle enough and close enough to a road to live on is only 4.7 percent of the city.
People can live only on the narrow valley floors along the rivers and roads.

steps.title: A city without a station
sentences: There is no railway station in the city.
The Utashinai Line was closed in 1988.
The nearest stations are Sunagawa and Takikawa to the west, about 10 km from the city center.

steps.title: A coal-mining town
sentences: Utashinai was born as a coal-mining town.
At its peak, around 1948, about 46,000 people lived here.
As the graph shows, from the 1960s the population fell off a cliff with each mine closure; after the closures of 1971, 1988 and 1995 it was down to 2,989 in 2020.

steps.title: Compared with the surroundings
sentences: Let's compare it with the surrounding area.
From 2000 to 2020, Utashinai's population halved.
Over the same period, the population within 20 km fell by 27 percent, and within 50 km by 16 percent.
The whole region is shrinking, but Utashinai stands out.

steps.title: How people make a living now
sentences: So what do people in Utashinai work at today?
In 2020, 1,150 people were working, 40 percent of those aged 15 and over.
The largest industry is medical care and welfare, with 226 people, one in five workers.
Next come wholesale and retail, construction, and public service.
Agriculture, forestry, fishing and mining, coal included, are down to just 27 people.

steps.title: Nine districts
sentences: The city is divided into nine districts, called aza.
The darker the green, the more people live there.
People live only in the northern valleys that open toward Sunagawa and Akabira.

steps.title: The center: Monju and Honcho
sentences: The center is Monju in the west and Honcho in the north.
These two districts hold 60 percent of the city's population.

steps.title: The fringe: four valley districts
sentences: Between them and up the valleys lie Kamui, Utagami, Nakamura and Kamiuta.
Their populations fell by 60 to 70 percent in 20 years.

steps.title: The exception: Toko
sentences: The exception is Toko.
Over 20 years its population barely changed, from 167 to 169.
Its share of children, 7.7 percent, is the highest in the city.
Women in their twenties and thirties increased from 9 to 16.

steps.title: Uninhabited: Shin-uta and Nishiyama
sentences: Shin-uta and Nishiyama in the south still have names, but nobody lived there even in 2000.
A third of the city is already land where no one lives.

steps.title: Work by district
sentences: Now let's look at work district by district.
In Honcho, where City Hall is, half of those aged 15 and over work, and many are in public service.
Toko also has a high share of workers, 46 percent, and 17 percent of them are in public service.
In Utagami and Kamui, on the other hand, only one in three people aged 15 and over works.

steps.title: From 2000 to 2020
sentences: Let's step from 2000 to 2020, five years at a time.
The color fades first in the far valleys.
The age charts change from a bulge in the middle to a top-heavy shape.

steps.title: Young women leave first
sentences: Who is leaving?
Women aged 20 to 39 fell from 502 to 135 in 20 years, a drop of 73 percent.
That is about one and a half times as fast as the population as a whole.
They leave in their early twenties for study or work, and again in their late twenties, for marriage and other reasons.

steps.title: No return in later life
sentences: Then, do people come back when they get older?
Following people in their fifties and sixties every five years, there was no period when their numbers grew.
Even after inheriting a house, hardly anyone seems to come back to live here.

steps.title: How work has changed
sentences: The kind of work has changed too.
The number of workers fell by almost half, from 2,183 in 2000 to 1,150 in 2020.
Construction fell sharply from 388 to 168, and manufacturing from 276 to 118.
Medical care and welfare, by contrast, fell only from 293 in 2005 to 226, and its share of workers rose from 16 to 20 percent.
Caring for the elderly is becoming the town's main work.

steps.title: Utashinai in 2050
sentences: If these trends continue, the population in 2050 is expected to be about 780, with around 20 children.
City-maintained roads would go from 13 meters per person today to about 50 meters.

steps.title: What is shared, and what is Utashinai's own
sentences: To sum up.
People disappear first from places far from the center, young women leave first, and the elderly do not come back.
This pattern is shared by depopulating areas across Hokkaido.
Having only coal as an industry, and dropping off a cliff with each mine closure, is shared by coal-mining towns.
And a valley terrain where only 4.7 percent of the land is livable is a condition unique to Utashinai.
